questions.q: What does the summary say happens to people who stay neutral on the new agenda?
a: They risk losing their jobs and destroying their careers
They are invited into a public debate
They face no consequences at work
They are protected by their employers
questions.why: Lesson 1 says even neutrality invites backlash, job loss and career damage.

questions.q: How does the summary describe corporations under this pressure?
a: They must follow political trends instead of pursuing profits
They fund both parties to stay safe
They withdraw from public debate entirely
They rely on courts to protect them
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues companies now adopt political positions to avoid being cancelled.

questions.q: What contradiction in 2020 does the summary use to show politics overriding science?
a: Large protests were allowed while gatherings were banned for pandemic reasons
Masks were required outdoors but not indoors
Scientists refused to comment on the virus
Governments lifted restrictions too early
questions.why: Lesson 2 points out that mass protests went ahead while other gatherings were prohibited.

questions.q: What happened to scientists who said men are on average taller than women?
a: They were fired for stating it
They were promoted for their honesty
They were asked to publish more research
They were ignored by the media
questions.why: Lesson 2 offers this as an example of politics pushing science aside.

questions.q: What is the foundation of democracy, according to the summary?
a: Freedom of speech and the free exchange of opinions
A fair and equal distribution of wealth
Regular elections with strong parties
A neutral and independent media
questions.why: Lesson 3 calls free expression the pylon of all democracies.
